references.text: Moses warns about prophets who speak in the Lord's name but whose words do not come true—a parallel warning against false prophets
The continuation of the warning against those who would lead Israel to follow other gods
Pharaoh's hardened heart and the signs performed in Egypt—showing that signs alone do not guarantee truth
Isaiah warns about those who make a covenant with lies and falsehood instead of trusting in the Lord
Jesus warns about false prophets and messiahs who will perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect
Paul describes the coming of the lawless one with the power of lies, signs, and wonders
The beast performs great signs and deceives the inhabitants of the earth with the signs it was allowed to perform
The prohibition against following other gods—a fundamental command that chapter 13 expands upon
John urges believers to test the spirits, for many false prophets have gone out into the world
